priceScope: Initial $15.38M annual diagnostic retained for comparison; current signed conditional channel has no finite positive price. Not complete portfolio EV or a verified marginal gift offer.

what: Crisis Intervention of Houston provides free, anonymous crisis counseling through telephone and teen text services.
Trained volunteers listen, help callers stabilize emotionally and connect them with other support.
Its programs also include suicide-bereavement groups, education and community crisis response.
strengths: Current recipient-owned pages identify a concrete local hotline and trained volunteer service.
Primary caller studies support a plausible short-term distress mechanism without treating calls as lives saved.
The recalibration preserves health and signed resources and distinguishes exposure from benefit.
reservations: Historical contacts are not current unique households, and 988 support may substitute.
Counselor-training evidence does not identify CIH-versus-988 QALYs or net earnings.
Full exposure burdens make the short-duration reference nonpositive; other programs and unpaid resources remain unmeasured.

sections.what: Crisis Intervention of Houston provides free, anonymous crisis counseling through telephone and teen text services. Trained volunteers listen, help callers stabilize emotionally and connect them with other support. Its programs also include suicide-bereavement groups, education and community crisis response.
sections.monitoring: The FY2024 return explicitly dates 35,812 calls, texts and chats to FY2022–2023; the current site's 3M since 1970 is cumulative. Neither supplies a current annual unique household cohort. Request deduplicated adult/teen callers, repeat contact, residence, alternative 988 use, referral uptake, completed follow-up, validated distress/utility measures, privacy/escalation harms and incremental volunteer hours. The .2 adult-household mapping and .9 Houston share remain judgments.
sections.qualitative: Gould 2007 followed 380 of 1,085 selected adult suicidal callers, with nonrandom attrition and no untreated comparator; improvement cannot fix CIH's causal fraction or utility duration. Gould 2013 examined 1,507 calls from 1,410 callers at 17 centers and found better end-call outcomes with ASIST-trained counselors: this compares counseling approaches, not hotline versus no care. Its Wiley abstract was read, not blocked PMC full text. Gould 2025 interviewed 437 adults at 12 centers in 2020–2021; perceived benefit is not measured mortality or a randomized effect. These primary studies support a short-term distress mechanism, not local causal QALYs or income coefficients. Existing 988, providers and family assistance remain the baseline. Recipient identity and owned donation form are unchanged; donation checkout/payee and current volunteer capacity need confirmation.
sections.cost: The initial $15.38M per better life remains a historical diagnostic, with 0.106330 clinical QALYs and +0.012011 income equivalents. The corrected reference retains all initial coefficients but applies full $2 one-off incremental time/access burden and .00001 health harm to all 7,162.4 distinct household proxies, not only 1,074.36 benefit-attributed proxies. Health is 0.051554 QALYs and signed income −0.261883 equivalents, total −0.210329; no finite positive current price follows. This conditional partial-channel reference is not evidence that CIH's whole portfolio harms people. Whole annual $181,993 expense is divided by limited hotline benefits; bereavement, education, crisis response and mortality channels remain unknown, not zero. The .3 clinical response, .02 utility, .02-year duration (7.3 days), .15 additionality and .9 local share remain judgments. Original studies do not justify more favorable local coefficients, so no price was forced. Positive total would require about 20.54 days at unchanged utility and other inputs; 13.5-day follow-up sensitivity is still nonpositive, while hypothetical one-month benefit gives $12.10M. A follow-up date is not observed benefit duration. Zero incremental time cost gives $16.26M but is only an alternative-burden sensitivity. $2 is per deduplicated household proxy beyond substitute service burdens, not per contact; $10/proxy represents $2 on each of five contacts implied by .2 mapping. The 53.718 resource-success proxies receive $100 net usable work/referral resources after taxes, benefits and alternative providers; overlap .5 adjusts only positive components before one household log, then full $2 cost. Other exposed proxies lose $2. No survivor wages or free-service retail value are counted. Benefit failure retains exposure burdens and harms; no exposure is distinct. Distinct payer/provider loss is localized once. Negative gains and harms are never overlap-discounted. Payer zero and $500,000 volunteer-inclusive expense are unverified hypotheses. Clinical-null, adverse, strong 988 substitution, unknown, finite duration, incidence and volunteer-cost cases remain testable.
sections.funding: FY2024 original recognized tax expense $181,993; FY2023 $181,602; FY2022 $226,567, all twelve-month June fiscal years. No populated event, rental or inventory expense addback recovered. Schedule D requests returned HTTP 404 rather than evidence of zero donated services. Unrecognized volunteers and partner care remain unknown. Historical FY2022–2023 contacts paired with FY2024 cost are an explicit mismatch. Whole-recipient cost versus this narrow hotline hypothesis is not a complete portfolio EV or verified marginal offer. No new volunteer-inclusive economic resource total, matched current unique cohort or funded marginal expansion was established. The $500,000 economic-cost sensitivity is not an observed budget.

model.costScope: Whole recognized annual tax recipient expense versus narrow historical hotline channel; unpaid/partner resources unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Local Houston reference with .9 judged MSA share; callers and teens not verified local adult households
model.formula: Exposed=N*unique; benefit union=exposed*b. Clinical=(clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse*q*discounted finite T − exposed*harm/onset discount)*g. Changed=union*success; one joint household log of overlap-adjusted positive net resources minus full costs; other exposed households retain full negative costs. Payer loss localized once. Current price=10*C/(health+signed income) only when positive. Historical-alpha-central reproduces complete initial health and income.
model.counterfactual: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, other hotlines, 911 when appropriate, community mental health and family support retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Services and accounting cost source-grounded; N historical contacts, not current unique people. All deduplication, additionality, utility, duration, income response and burden coefficients remain judgments. Primary studies do not identify CIH's causal increment versus 988. Current total nonpositive; omitted portfolio channels and next-gift response unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional short-term stabilization and useful support linkage; contacts not deaths prevented
